st: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix the coconut milk, onion and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Cut off the thick stems of the taro leaves.
Stack several leaves in the center of a banana leaf or foil sheet.
Make a bowl shape with the leaves and pour in half the coconut mixture.
Fold the leaves over to enclose and wrap tightly in banana leaf and foil.
Bake on a tray for [[45 minutes]] until the leaves are soft.
Open the parcel and spoon over the remaining coconut milk.
Return to the oven for [[10 minutes]] and serve.

ing: fresh sushi-grade tuna or white fish
st: Use only very fresh fish labeled safe to eat raw. Keep it cold.
Cut the fish into small cubes and put in a bowl.
Pour over the juice of 5 limes and add [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Chill for [[30 minutes]] until the fish turns opaque.
Drain off most of the lime juice.
Add the onion, tomato, cucumber and chili.
Pour in [[0.75 cup]] chilled coconut milk and stir gently.
Serve right away, chilled.
Soak the noodles in hot water for 15 minutes, then drain and cut into shorter lengths.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pan over high heat.
Brown the beef for 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, [[1 tbsp]] ginger and onion and cook 3 minutes.
Add the carrots, [[0.25 cup]] soy sauce, [[2 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Simmer for [[10 minutes]] until the beef is tender.
Add the noodles and stir through.
Cook for 5 minutes until the noodles absorb the sauce.
Taste, adjust soy sauce and serve hot.
Stir [[2.25 tsp]] yeast into [[1 cup]] warm milk with [[1 tbsp]] sugar and rest 10 minutes.
Mix [[4 cups]] flour, [[0.5 cup]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt, then add the yeast milk, the egg and [[4 tbsp]] soft butter.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise for [[60 minutes]] until doubled.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Divide into 12 balls and arrange in a greased baking dish.
Whisk [[2 cans]] coconut milk, [[1 cup]] sugar and [[1 tbsp]] cornstarch together.
Pour the sauce over and around the buns.
Bake for [[35 minutes]] until golden and the sauce is thick.
Rinse [[1 cup]] rice until the water runs clear.
Put the rice, [[3 cups]] water and the orange leaves in a pot.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] cocoa and [[0.5 cup]] sugar.
Add the coconut milk and a pinch of salt.
Simmer 15 more minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Fish out and throw away the orange leaves.
Serve the rice pudding warm in small bowls.
Stir [[2.25 tsp]] yeast and [[1 tbsp]] sugar into [[0.75 cup]] warm milk and rest 10 minutes.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, remaining sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Add the yeast milk, egg and [[2 tbsp]] oil. Knead 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise [[60 minutes]].
Divide into 8 balls and flatten to discs about 1/2 inch thick.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil to 350°F (175°C).
Fry each disc 2 minutes per side until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
Cut the peeled bananas in half crosswise.
Boil in [[4 cups]] lightly salted water for [[20 minutes]] until just tender.
Drain the cooked bananas in a colander.
Heat the coconut milk with the onion in a saucepan over medium heat.
Simmer gently until slightly thickened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in [[0.5 tsp]] salt and taste the sauce.
Put the bananas into the sauce and warm through 3 minutes.
Serve the bananas and sauce warm.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C), standing in for the hot stones.
Season the pork and fish with [[2 tsp]] salt.
Wrap the pork in banana leaves, then foil.
Wrap the fish separately with a spoonful of coconut cream.
Wrap the taro and breadfruit in banana leaves and foil.
Put the pork and taro in a deep roasting tray.
Cover with a layer of wet banana leaves and foil.
Bake for [[2 hours]], then add the breadfruit and fish.
Bake another [[50 minutes]] until the pork reaches 145°F (63°C) and the fish is flaky.
Rest 10 minutes, unwrap and serve.
